verdict.rationale: Cursor's docs describe an end-to-end issue-to-PR flow. Automations and cloud agents can be triggered by Linear and other tracker events, using the example of 'a ticket created in Linear triggering a cloud agent to implement a feature'. The agent then builds and verifies the change in an isolated VM and opens a pull request with artifacts attached. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the issue-to-PR flow, explicit documentation of GitHub Issues (not just Linear) as a trigger source.

support.subject: As a developer, I can turn a tracked issue into a complete pull request end-to-end

citations.quote: A ticket created in Linear triggering a cloud agent to implement a feature
Cursor Automations run cloud agents in the background, either on a schedule or in response to events from GitHub, GitLab, Slack, webhooks, Linear, and more.
make coordinated changes, and open pull requests in the repos it changes
Agents can start dev servers, open the app in a browser, click through UI flows, and verify their changes work before pushing a PR.
These artifacts are attached to the PR so you can quickly validate changes without checking out the branch locally.
